title: New 'Go Get Married' Map Reveals Provo Region Has Highest New Marriage Rate In US | Institute for Family Studies
gist: A new interactive IFS mapping project finds the Provo, Utah area has the highest rate of new marriages among young adults in the US—an estimated 132 first-time marriages per 1,000 never-married adults ages 22-39 annually (2020-2024)—followed by Fort Wayne, Indiana (106) and Evansville/southwest Indiana (94).

insights.claim: An IFS interactive mapping project estimates the Provo, Utah area averaged 132 first-time marriages annually per 1,000 never-married adults ages 22-39 from 2020 to 2024, the highest new-marriage rate among young adults in the United States.
insights.speaker: Aubree Hudson
insights.so_what: Concentration of household formation in specific metros flags where family-linked housing and consumer demand is structurally strongest.
insights.quote: an average of 132 first-time marriages occurred annually for every 1,000 never-married adults ages 22–39 in the Provo area from 2020 to 2024

insights.claim: The Fort Wayne area of Indiana ranked second in new-marriage rate with 106 marriages per 1,000 never-married adults, followed by Evansville and southwest Indiana with 94.
insights.speaker: Aubree Hudson
insights.so_what: The top-ranked regions cluster in Utah and Indiana, reinforcing an interior/middle-America concentration of marriage that diverges from coastal metros.
insights.quote: The Fort Wayne area and its southern suburbs in Indiana ranked second with 106 marriages per 1,000 never-married adults, followed by Evansville and southwest Indiana with 94
